[engine] When a change reroutes the code path that hosts a counter, that counter's zero is not evidence of absence: prove the instrument still runs on the layers being claimed before quoting any of its values.

<!-- generated by harness_engine/build_memories.py from traces/lessons.jsonl -->
<!-- lesson_id: eng-gate-0003 | class: gate-integrity | superseded_by: - -->

**class**: `gate-integrity`

## 為什麼（because）

CGC_SLOT_TABLE_GPU builds the GPU table INSTEAD of the host remap leaf -- llama-graph.cpp:2178-2242 is an if/else, so for il >= CGC_S1_MIN_IL the leaf is never created and cache_remap_tensors[il] stays empty. The ONE increment of cache->n_zero_mapped_selected (llama-context.cpp:5475) sits inside the leaf-write block, which the hook skips when remap == nullptr. Every served layer therefore stops reporting the 'a selected expert read the ZERO slot' quality leak, and the teardown line (llama-expert-cache.cpp:2229) prints n_zero_mapped_selected=0 -- byte-identical to a run with no leak. The S1 A/B is documented as a pure scheduler/dispatch change; this monitoring change it carries silently is not in that description, and a gate that reads that counter would pass for the wrong reason. Note the code comment at llama-context.h:364 claims the opposite ('the leaf itself is still built when this is on'), which is how the trap survived review.
